description: Hand-verified support subgraph for the multi-hop and aggregation queries. For each query: the required documents, the joining or aggregated entities, and the facts a complete answer needs. fidelity_row() reads this file; it diagnoses extraction coverage and never decides the gate.

The default `watermark_delay_s` is 30 seconds; the minimum accepted value is 5 seconds.

The pipeline used the default watermark delay, but the transform buffered output for 90 seconds, so records stamped just before the buffered flush were already below the watermark when they reached the sink stage.
The pipeline had no consumer for the late-data side output, so the records routed there were discarded rather than delivered.

The tracker embeds the watermark in every state checkpoint, so a restart resumes from the last committed position instead of replaying the whole window, and it emits a `watermark_lag` gauge every 10 batches.
The fix caps transform buffering at half the watermark delay and fails validation when a transform declares a longer buffer.
The SecretRotationJob re-reads the file every 15 minutes and swaps a credential in place when its version changes, without restarting the pipeline.
The credential file had been rotated at 08:40, but the pipeline was configured for ephemeral runs, so the SecretRotationJob was not active and the in-memory credential remained the expired one.
The SecretRotationJob re-reads the file every 15 minutes and swaps a credential in place when its version changes, without restarting the pipeline.
A swap takes effect from the next batch onward; in-flight batches keep the old credential.
The fix makes validation warn when a long-running ephemeral pipeline uses a file-backed credential.
When a pipeline has not acknowledged a position within `cdc_slot_ttl_hours` -- default 24 hours -- the slot is released, and the next start performs a full snapshot instead of resuming.
The pipelines had been paused for maintenance for 31 hours, so their slots had been released and the database had already reclaimed their WAL.

The PostgresSource uses the logical-replication slot named by its `slot` argument and confirms its log position once per committed checkpoint; the database retains WAL segments the slot has not confirmed.
A pipeline that checkpoints rarely therefore holds WAL longer than a short commit interval would suggest.
The fix requires an explicit `cdc_pause_acknowledged: true` before a pause longer than the retention window is planned.
Batch payloads are compressed with `compression.codec`, which defaults to `zstd` at level 3.
gzip's decompression cost more CPU per byte than zstd, and the team had assumed the two were comparable.
Compression is applied after batching and before encryption.
The fix adds a `compression.min_throughput_mbps` warning when a downgraded codec is in use.
When the limit is reached, producers block for up to `quota_wait_s`, which defaults to 20 seconds, before the batch is rejected as `quota_exceeded`.
Raising the per-pipeline limit had no effect because the binding constraint was the per-group tenant quota.
Quota consumption is released when the sink acknowledges the batch, not when the batch is produced.
The fix adds a warning when one pipeline in a group accounts for more than 60% of the group's in-flight batches.
Entries are append-only and are retained in the active store for 400 days, after which they are archived to cold storage; archived entries remain queryable through the `quorva audit` command.
Verification tools must accept both formats; an entry whose digest length matches neither format is rejected.
Each entry carries at least the actor identity, the resource, the action, and a digest of the request body; some authentication methods add their own identifiers.
On 1 December 2026 the AuditTrail digest changes from a SHA-256 digest truncated to 128 bits to the full 256-bit digest.
Entries written before that date remain verifiable with the old format and are not rewritten.
The CutoverController shifts traffic between blue and green fleets in steps controlled by `cutover_step_percent`, which defaults to 10 percent.
Each step is held for `cutover_hold_s` (default 300 seconds) while error rate and p99 latency are compared against the stable fleet.
Latency was not part of the automatic rollback condition, so the controller kept stepping forward and the operator kept rolling back manually.
A step is rolled back automatically when the new fleet's error rate exceeds the stable fleet's by more than 2 percentage points.
The fix adds a latency ratio to the rollback condition and refuses a manual rollback within one hold window of the previous one.
A BackfillPlan splits a requested date range into segments of at most 6 hours and runs them at `backfill_concurrency`, which defaults to 2.
The requested range ended two hours after the watermark, but the plan had been started with the overlap check disabled by an operator flag.
The sink's idempotency keys covered live writes but not backfill segments, so the duplicates were not collapsed.
The plan refuses to start when the target sink's current watermark overlaps the requested range, because the replay would duplicate live records.
The fix removes the override flag so an overlapping range cannot start, and gives each backfill segment its own idempotency namespace so a retried segment collapses instead of duplicating.
